dominant_breach: manufactured housing can appear to create low-cost ownership while the resident often owns a depreciable or hard-to-move home but rents the land, leaving home equity exposed to lot-rent escalation, eviction, finance constraints, and community sale
fastest_washout: lot-rent increases, land-lease nonrenewal, chattel-loan terms, moving infeasibility, park sale, and weak resident-purchase rights convert ownership into a stranded asset

rental_market_power_gate.note: The home/land split creates a landlord-market-power channel inside nominal homeownership.

manufactured_housing_land_lease_split.note: The home/land split means nominal homeownership cannot certify as wealth formation unless land tenure, lease renewal, rent escalation, eviction, and community-sale protections are proven.

manufactured_home_mobility_lock_in.note: Moving a manufactured home is often infeasible or value-destructive; active scoring treats lot-rent escalation and nonrenewal as possible equity washout events.

manufactured_lot_rent_escalation.note: Recent survey/context evidence makes lot-rent and no-lease exposure a direct wealth-retention risk, not a merely theoretical affordability concern.

resident_purchase_opportunity.note: Resident-purchase or preservation rights must be scored for timing, financing, notice, and enforceability before community sale converts ownership into a stranded asset.

chattel_finance_protection_gap.note: Personal-property financing and limited mortgage channels can leave manufactured-home buyers with weaker protections and higher costs than real-property borrowers.

title_probate_finality.note: Title, fixture, and land-ownership status affect resale, inheritance, and legal finality.

housing_market_power_remedy_access.note: The cube needs jurisdiction-level data on rent-increase limits, lease renewal rights, eviction protection, and resident-purchase enforcement.

proof_debt: share of manufactured homeowners renting lots by jurisdiction and owner type
lot-rent escalation, nonrenewal, and eviction incidence
mobility costs, resale haircut, and abandonment risk after rent increases or park sale
chattel-loan terms and protections compared with mortgage loans
resident-purchase opportunity coverage, financing, and success rates

gate_02_floor_reality.why: Manufactured housing can provide a low-cost floor only if lot-rent and finance terms do not consume the affordability advantage.

gate_03_threshold_moments.why: Purchase, lease signing, rent increase, park sale, default, and attempted move are threshold moments where home equity can be stranded.

gate_05_washout_reconcentration.why: Lot-rent escalation and land control can reconcentrate the value created by low-cost homeownership into landowner revenue.

gate_09_conversion_rails_claim_finality.why: Chattel, title, fixture, and land-lease status determine whether the resident has durable ownership or a fragile occupancy claim.

gate_15_place_public_finance_service_wea.why: Manufactured-home communities are place assets; infrastructure, zoning, public finance, and preservation rules determine whether they remain affordable.

gate_16_household_market_extraction_cost.why: Lot rent, utility pass-throughs, financing costs, and moving infeasibility make recurring costs a wealth trap.

gate_18_fresh_start_capacity_post_shock_.why: Default, eviction, or park sale can leave residents with a stranded asset and weak recovery path.

gate_19_intergenerational_transfer_famil.why: Home value cannot serve as family wealth unless title, resale, inheritance, and land tenure are durable.
